title: SynoRing R1 — Gesture Control Ring for AR & Smart Glasses
excerpt: SynoRing R1 is a gesture control ring for AR and smart glasses. Tap, glide, and circle to control what you see. Pre-order for $99, shipping Q1 2027.
content_html:
Control your AR glasses, smart glasses, headset, phone, laptop, PC, or robot without breaking the moment.

Your world, at your fingertips.

Discover SynoRing

SynoRing turns finger movements and thumb touches
into controls for your AR glasses.

Meet SynoRing

A gesture controller.
Made to feel natural.

For your spatial world

AR control.
Without the interruption.

Your AR glasses.
Controlled from your ring.

Select with a tap. Scroll with a glide. Adjust with a circle.

01 / Input

Touch + movement

Thumb touches and finger motion work together. Tap, glide, hold, or circle to control what is in view.

02 / Experience

A smaller gesture

Designed for subtle control at your side, without speaking a command or reaching toward a floating screen.

03 / Application

Made for spatial apps

Explore music, reading, and navigation today in our interactive browser demo.

Interactive demo

See through the glasses.
Control it with the ring.

  • Tap to select
  • Glide to scroll
  • Circle to adjust
  • Hold for apps

Try the demo

One ring.
So many ways to stay present.

Your music.
Your moment.

Adjust the volume. Keep your rhythm.

Follow the thought.
Not the screen.

Move through a page with a glide.

Eyes up.
World open.

Your next direction, a tap away.

Motion and touch.
Working together.

Sensors read your movement. Touch gives it intent.

The connection

From a small gesture
to an action in view.

Our integration direction connects ring input to spatial applications through a phone-side software layer. Device support will be confirmed through testing.

  2. 02

  3. 03

    Your AR app

    Select, scroll, and adjust

For developers

Your app.
A new way in.

Building a spatial reader, a media interface, or something we have not imagined? Help shape how ring input fits your application.

Build with SynoRing

TapSelect a track

GlideMove through a page

CircleBring a map closer

Your context defines the action.

Get closer to
the first SynoRing.

Join the waitlist for launch updates and developer pilots.

A little more to know.

When can I get SynoRing?

Early means early. SynoRing R1 is open for pre-order and estimated to ship in Q1 2027, with free shipping within the US. Join the waitlist to follow developer pilots and production updates.24

Which AR glasses will it work with?

Compatibility is being explored. Our direction is a phone-side SDK that connects with AR ecosystems. Supported devices will be announced after validation.

Can I get involved as a developer?

We would love to hear from people building spatial interfaces. Tell us what you are working on.
